summary: Rumley Lookout, first in Sumter County; moved in 2005 to Perry Lakes Park, Perry County, and rebuilt as a bird-watching tower without its cab.

facts.design: Aermotor MC-39 tower, rebuilt without its cab
facts.status_note: Moved in 2005 from Sumter County to Perry Lakes Park, Perry County; rebuilt without its cab.

events.note: Register gives 1936 as the build year; its text says the CCC erected the tower in the late 1930s.
Removed from Sumter County to Perry Lakes Park, Perry County.
Moved and restored by students from Judson College and Auburn University's Rural Studio, with help from the Alabama Forestry Commission and Perry County.
Rebuilt without its 7-by-7-foot cab, for an open-sky canopy effect for bird-watching.
Listed on the National Historic Lookout Register on December 16, 2009.

corrections.why: The record's point is the original Sumter County site. The register places the tower at Perry Lakes Park, Perry County, since 2005, and the Sumter County site no longer has it.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1936 as the build year and says the CCC erected the tower in the late 1930s. Both fall in the same decade, so the story gives both.
The Forest Lookouts listing names the Alabama Forestry Commission for the Rumley tower in Sumter County. The register names the Perry County Commission as administrator at Perry Lakes Park.

notes_for_editor: Access is not set: no source gives opening hours or climbing terms for Perry Lakes Park. The register's 148 ft (45 m) figure is the park's elevation, not the tower height; height_m uses the 100-foot tower figure. Lead, not used in the story: the Alabama Forestry Commission history PDF lists CCC Camp P-73 at York, AL, from May 1934 to October 1938, in Sumter County. No source ties that camp to this tower. The Rumley-to-Perry Lakes move is the only fact-level conflict; the story presents both build descriptions.
